name: Ghosts of the Gridiron — game line-ups, officials, honours and a roster limit
attribution: Ghosts of the Gridiron, John J. Fenton, 2004-2008
rights: A copyrighted personal website by a named author, preserved from the Wayback Machine. FACTS are ingested and cited to the snapshot; prose is not reproduced; images are held pending permission and none is published.
_what: The seventeen pages of the 243 that carry a GAME LINE-UP, plus the two that carry an honours list, the officials named on them, and one Eastern League roster limit.
_why_started_a_game_and_not_a_probable_l: The 1926 Bears-Tigers programme printed its line-up BEFORE kickoff, which is why programme.probable_lineup exists: a man named there was expected to start and might not have. These are GAME ACCOUNTS printed AFTER the whistle, in the Bethlehem Globe-Times and the Philadelphia Public Ledger. A man named in one started. The distinction is the printing order, not the shape of the table.
_a_substitution_is_a_different_assertion: A man who came on did NOT start. The 53 substitutions are held under ghosts.substitution and are never folded into the elevens; folding them would make the archive unable to tell a starter from a replacement, which is the only thing these pages are precise about.
_officials_are_people: Under the standing rule of 2026-09-08: the line is on-field game participants. The AFFILIATION IS TAKEN AS PRINTED -- `Wheeler, Haverford` -- because it is the source's own words and this ingest does not know whether Haverford is where he studied, where he coached or where he was from.
_the_eastern_league_stays_excluded: Bethlehem Bears and Gilberton Catamounts are already in the club table under EFL, holding nobody. Naming men on a club the table holds is NOT admitting the league, and no club is created here.
_clubs_not_in_the_table_stay_out: REWRITTEN 2026-09-11. This used to name TEN clubs, and the report beside it named fifteen; both were typed by hand and both were short, because the store never recorded which club a refused side was -- it counted the men under the PAGE FILENAME. Counted from each page's printed title there are SEVENTEEN clubs the table does not hold: All-Lancaster, Shenandoah, Holmesburg A.C., Conshohocken A.C., Bethlehem Blue Stars, Kaywood C.C., Corley Catholic Club, Reliance Field Club, Deaf Mutes, Bridesburg, Chesbrook, Parkside A.C., USS Michigan, Washington Pros, New York Shipyard, Hog Island, Merchant Ship. They are REPORTED, not minted, and their sides are NOT declared (Ryan, 2026-09-11): admitting them is a separate ruling. Some are athletic clubs and some are service teams, and those are different questions.
_frankford_1902_is_held_not_declared: Frankford_Mutes_1902.htm prints `Frankford A. A.`. The club table holds `club-frankford-yellow-jackets-1899`, named `Frankford Yellow Jackets` 1899-1906 from the Frankford Yellow Jackets book, and carries no name `Frankford A. A.`. Declaring this side onto that club would ANSWER the lineage question Ryan holds open -- whether Frankford A.A. in 1902 is the archive's early Frankford -- by implication. Held until he rules. Its men stay counted under the filename, and gate G7 stays red on it, which is the point.
_pages_declared_before_the_reader_fix: Read by gate_ghosts_lineups G6. On 2026-09-11 the reader moved out of a dead session's /tmp into src/measure_ghosts_lineups.py and was fixed for hyphenated backs, `L. H.`/`R. H.`, the backfield's printed order and bracketed names. These three pages were already declared and already placed 25 men; the fix must not move a single man on them. The baseline is build-reports/ghosts-lineups.before-reader-fix-2026-09-11.json, the measurement exactly as it stood.
_the_photograph_is_refused: Bethlehem_Gooch.htm carries a portrait credited 'Image courtesy, Beth Campanella'. A named private lender is not a licence. Recorded as a refusal so a later reader can see it was seen and declined rather than missed.
_citation: The newspaper where the page names one; Fenton as the FINDING AID and not the source of the fact; the Wayback snapshot address and its sha256.
_the_narrative_prose_is_NOT_in_this_pass: 2,444 name-shaped strings across 229 pages, measured at 1.3% carrying enough context to be usable. Parked because prose extraction is an undesigned capability that would touch the media guides and the reference books too -- NOT because there is nothing there. On the open list in docs/ARCHIVE_CONTEXT.md.
_why_the_side_to_club_map_is_declared: It could not be derived safely. The line-up header is `ClubA | position | ClubB` in the table pages and a bare run of words in the prose pages, and a reader that took the two capitalised strings before the first position picked up the first PLAYER as the second club on 16 of 17 pages. Rather than tune a parser until it agrees with what I already read, the three pages that touch a club the table holds are declared here WITH THE PRINTED EVIDENCE. The other fourteen name no club the table holds, so no map is needed for them. -- WRONG, found 2026-09-11: three of those fourteen DO touch a club the table holds -- Frankford 1902, Frankford 1922, and Frankford against Dayton in 1924, an NFL game where the table holds both clubs. The sentence was never checked, and nothing could check it: an unmapped page wrote no claim for G2 to look at. 1922 and 1924 are declared below (Ryan, 2026-09-11); 1902 is held, see _frankford_1902_is_held_not_declared.

Yellowjackets_Thanksgiving_1924.htm._the_title_and_the_date_disagree: The page title reads `Yellow Jackets vs. Dayton Triangles, Thanksgiving Day, 1925`. The article is The Philadelphia Record, November 28, 1924, and the filename says 1924. Held as printed, both; not resolved here. The year this ingest uses is the filename's, which agrees with the dateline.
